issue: A repeated or non-string q is not rejected. String() turns ?q=a&q=b into 'a,b' and ?q[x]=1 into '[object Object]', and both get searched, where the spec requires 400 { error: 'Query must be a single string' }.
evidence: `const q = String(req.query.q ?? '').trim();` has no typeof check -> GET /api/books/search?q=a&q=b returns 200 [] instead of 400

issue: Off-by-one: `>=` rejects a trimmed query of exactly 100 characters. The spec allows 100 and rejects only 101 or more (AC6).
evidence: `if (q.length >= MAX_QUERY_LENGTH)` with MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 100 -> q='a'.repeat(100) returns 400 instead of 200

issue: The underscore is not escaped, so `_` is still a LIKE single-character wildcard on title (AC8). The spec requires escaping \, % and _.
evidence: `query.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/%/g, '\\%')` has no `_` replacement -> q=_ matches every non-empty title and returns all books instead of []

issue: Author is matched with case-sensitive `instr(author, ?)` instead of `LIKE ? ESCAPE '\'`. This breaks case-insensitive author search (AC2/AC3) and the spec's rule to use LIKE ... ESCAPE on both columns.
evidence: `WHERE title LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\' OR instr(author, ?) > 0` with params [pattern, query] -> q=fowler does not match seed author 'Martin Fowler', so 'Refactoring' is missing from the results
